name: Grandpa Kolyo's Oak (Studena)

location.address: Field southeast of Studena village, right of the road entering from Svilengrad, Svilengrad Municipality, Haskovo Province, Bulgaria

access: Stands in a field beside the entrance road to the village, visible from the whole village and from the road; the field is private farmland (owner named after), so view from the roadside.
transport: Svilengrad municipality village; by car from Svilengrad, public transport not checked.
verify_notes:
- Species: contest entry says English oak (Quercus robur); Bulgarian press calls it 'summer oak' (летен дъб), which is the usual Bulgarian name for Q. robur. Taken from the contest, not independently checked.
- Bulgaria 'Tree with Roots 2021' winner (737 votes, awarded 1 Feb 2022 per Svilengrad municipality) and Bulgaria's entry to European Tree of the Year 2022 (24,431 votes, 14th).
- Named for landowner Nikola Dimitrov Angelov ('Grandpa Kolyo'), who rested under it; tradition says it descends from the dense forest that once covered the area; a cross was erected nearby in 2019.
- Age 350 years is local tradition and the contest figure, not measured. No girth or height found on the municipality page; contest page not fetched.
- Alive: 2022 municipality and Darik articles; lifecheck NONE (nothing geotagged). Flagged.
- Pin: only the contest GPS, not cross-checked against a map: approximate.
- Sources are the municipality and the contest chain (one origin); no independent second source.
story:
Grandpa Kolyo used to rest under this oak, and the village of Studena named it after him. He was Nikola Dimitrov Angelov, and the field where it stands, at the entrance to the village on the road from Svilengrad, was his.

Local tradition gives the tree about 350 years and says it is a survivor of the dense forest that once covered this corner of south-eastern Bulgaria. That is tradition rather than record. The age comes from the village and from the contest entry, and nobody has published a girth or a height. If you have stood beside it with a tape measure, tell us.

It is visible from the whole village and from the road in. In 2019 a cross was put up nearby. Two years later the oak won Bulgaria's Tree with Roots contest for 2021 with 737 votes, and in 2022 it represented the country in European Tree of the Year, finishing 14th with 24,431 votes.

The field is private farmland. See the oak from the roadside, which is where the village sees it from too.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the lone oak in the field to the right of the road as you enter Studena from Svilengrad, visible from the whole village.
not_merged_reason: Not merged: no honest container. Single tree on private farmland, view from the road only, but the only pin is the contest GPS of the trunk rather than a roadside viewing point; no girth or height; sources are one origin (municipality plus contest). Does not pass the single-famous-tree test on its own. Publish once a roadside viewing pin and a second independent source exist, or when a Svilengrad/Haskovo place with four trees opens.

name: The Venerable Oak of Novo Selo

location.address: Village centre, in front of the five-spout fountain, Novo Selo, Veliko Tarnovo Municipality, Bulgaria

access: Free; stands in the centre of the village by a public fountain (press and search summaries; not seen on a map).
transport: Village near Veliko Tarnovo; distance and bus not checked, treat as a car trip.
verify_notes:
- Bulgaria 'Tree with Roots 2019' winner (1,073 votes per news.bg, 17 Dec 2019); Bulgaria's entry to European Tree of the Year 2020.
- Age 'about 500 years' is stated by press (BNR headline '500-year-old oak', 'according to specialists' in a search summary I could not open); news.bg only says it has kept the village's history since its founding in 1750, which is a tension: the tree is claimed older than the village. Do not link the two. No measurement seen; girth and height not found in any source I reached.
- Fountain detail (five spouts of cold water in front of the oak) and the 2010 planting of a young oak grown from its acorn beside it, so the roots intertwine: from a search summary of BNR/contest text, not a fetched page. Treat as lead until seen.
- Species from contest entry (Quercus robur); press says only 'oak'.
- Alive: news.bg Dec 2019 (article says an arborist assessment will follow); Commons photo dated 2019-09-26/2020 at the coordinate (lifecheck OLD). Nothing later found: flagged.
- Pin: contest GPS only; the site is a village-centre landmark so probably good to a few metres, but not cross-checked.
story:
The village of Novo Selo, near Veliko Tarnovo, dates its founding to 1750. The oak in its centre is said to be about 500 years old, which would make the tree older than the village by a couple of centuries.

Those two numbers do not come from the same place, and it is worth keeping them apart. The founding date is the village's own history. The 500 years comes from Bulgarian press reports citing specialists, and nobody has published a measurement, a ring count, a girth or a height. So the honest version is simpler: a big old oak that the village regards as the keeper of its history since 1750, of an age nobody has settled. If you know more, tell us.

It stands in the middle of the village, a landmark rather than a secret. In December 2019 it won Bulgaria's Tree with Roots contest with 1,073 votes, and in 2020 it was the country's entry to European Tree of the Year. At the time an arborist's assessment was promised, and we have found no report of it since.

The contest entry names it as a pedunculate oak; the press says only oak.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the big old oak in the centre of Novo Selo, the village's landmark tree, standing in the village centre by a public fountain.
not_merged_reason: Not merged: no honest container. Single village tree with no measurement, pin from the contest GPS only, latest proof of life 2019/2020, and its most distinctive details (the five-spout fountain, the 2010 acorn-grown oak beside it) come from search summaries not yet seen on a fetched page. Does not pass the single-famous-tree test on its own. Publish if a Veliko Tarnovo place opens (the village is roughly 20 km west) or once a post-2020 life check and a fetched source land.
